description: Figure 2 is a grouped bar chart that compares the accuracy of different models across three distinct natural language processing tasks: Sentiment Accuracy (labeled “Sentiment Acc”), STS Accuracy (labeled “STS Acc”), and Paraphrase Accuracy (labeled “Paraphrase Acc”). The horizontal axis lists five model configurations: “Single-task_Baseline,” “Baseline_with_Adaptive_Dropout,” “Unsupervised_SimCSE,” “Supervised_SimCSE,” and “2-Tier SimCSE.” For each model, three adjacent vertical bars represent its performance on the three tasks, color-coded as light orange for Sentiment Acc, pink for STS Acc, and light blue for Paraphrase Acc. The vertical axis, labeled “Accuracy / Correlation,” ranges from 0.0 to 0.8 in increments of 0.2. The chart shows that “2-Tier SimCSE” achieves the highest accuracy across all three tasks, with values approximately 0.65 for Sentiment Acc, 0.78 for STS Acc, and 0.75 for Paraphrase Acc. In contrast, the “Single-task_Baseline” model performs the lowest overall, with accuracies around 0.55, 0.50, and 0.70 respectively. The bars are grouped by model, allowing direct comparison of performance across tasks for each model, and the chart visually emphasizes the consistent improvement of the 2-Tier SimCSE approach over other configurations.
